title: A team member's turn never speaks with George's voice allowance, never falls back to his assistant, and is never cut off by someone else's
requested_outcome:
An independent review of the team build (PR #73, 1 October) found three gaps in how a team member's turn runs. Fix all three; change nothing for the owner's turns.
(1) /turn honours speak=true and transcribes uploaded audio for a staff request (crooks-assistant/app/routes/turn.py), spending the owner's ElevenLabs allowance, although /speak itself refuses staff. For a request the door made a staff request (app/tools/authority.current() is STAFF), ignore `speak` (no text-to-speech is generated and the answer says nothing about audio) and refuse an audio upload with a 403 in the route's own refusal shape, saying in words that the team types to CLIVE.
(2) Runtime.provider_for (crooks-assistant/app/runtime.py) returns the OWNER's assistant for a staff request when no staff provider factory is set. Fail closed instead: a staff request with no factory raises, and /turn answers it with a refusal, never the owner's assistant.
(3) ensure_started calls _stop_retired on every turn, so a team member's assistant replaced because their card changed is stopped on anyone's next turn, even while a turn is still running in it. Stop a retired assistant only once no turn is running in it (count turns in flight per provider, or stop it when its last running turn ends); never stop one mid-turn.
acceptance_criteria: A staff /turn with speak=true produces no text-to-speech call (the voice client is never asked) and returns the text answer; the owner's /turn with speak=true still speaks.
A staff /turn with an audio upload is refused with 403 and words saying the team types to CLIVE; the transcriber is never called.
With staff_provider_factory unset, a staff request never reaches runtime.provider: provider_for raises and /turn returns a refusal.
A retired team assistant with a turn in flight is not stopped by another person's turn; it is stopped once that turn ends.
The new behaviour is proven in crooks-assistant/tests/test_staff_turn_hardening.py, and it passes; no existing test changes.
